conversation.content:
Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I'm here to support you during this significant time in your life. As we navigate the ups and downs of new motherhood together, I want to assure you that our conversation will be a safe and confidential space for you to express yourself freely.

As part of our assessment today, we'll be using the EPDS, which is a tool designed to help us understand how you're feeling and identify any potential concerns that might be impacting your well-being during the postpartum period. The EPDS screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it's a valuable resource in helping us provide the best possible care for you.

Please know that everything we discuss will remain confidential, and I'm here to listen without judgment. My goal is to create a supportive environment where you feel comfortable sharing your thoughts and feelings. We'll take this assessment one question at a time, and I'll guide you through the process. The EPDS consists of 10 questions, and we'll work through each one together.

Let's get started, shall we? The first question is about how you've been feeling over the past week. Can you tell me a little bit about how you've been managing your emotions lately? Have you been able to enjoy the things you usually like to do, or have you been feeling overwhelmed?

.. I'm not sure where to start. I mean, I'm happy to be here and talk about this, I guess. It's just been really tough lately. I feel like I'm running on empty all the time. Taking care of the baby is exhausting, and some days I feel like I'm just going through the motions. I used to love doing things like reading and taking walks, but lately, I just haven't had the energy or interest. It's not that I don't enjoy spending time with my baby, it's just that everything feels so overwhelming. 

Sometimes I get really anxious about the baby's health, like if she's eating enough or if she's too hot or cold. It's like, I know I'm doing my best, but I just can't shake the feeling that I'm not doing enough. And some days, I just feel really sad for no reason. It's not all the time, but it's enough to make me feel like something's wrong with me. I don't know, maybe I'm just tired and that's all it is. But it's hard to explain. I just feel like I'm not myself right now, and it's scary. 

I do try to manage, though. I mean, I get up every day and take care of my baby, and my partner is really supportive. But sometimes, when it's just me and the baby at home, I feel really alone and like I'm just trying to survive until my partner gets home from work. Does that make sense.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Yeah... I'd say that's still there for me, but not as much as it used to be. I mean, I can still laugh and find the humor in things, but it's just not as easy as it was before. Some days, it feels like it takes a lot more effort to find the funny side of things. And even when I do laugh, it's not always as genuine as it used to be. It's like, I'm laughing on the outside, but on the inside, I'm still feeling kind of... flat, I guess.

But it's not like I've completely lost my sense of humor or anything. I still enjoy watching comedies or reading funny stories, and I can still appreciate a good joke. It's just that, lately, it feels like I have to work a bit harder to get to that place where I can really laugh and enjoy myself. And sometimes, even when I'm laughing, I'll catch myself feeling a little sad or anxious underneath, which is weird. It's like, my mind is still worried about all the things that could go wrong, even when I'm trying to have fun. Does that make sense.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Honestly, that's not really been me lately. I mean, I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but now it just feels like... I don't know, everything feels like a chore, I guess. Even things that I used to enjoy, like going out with friends or trying new restaurants, just don't seem as appealing to me right now.

I think part of it is just the exhaustion, you know? Taking care of a new baby is just so all-consuming, and it's hard to think about anything else. But even when I do have some downtime, I just don't seem to have the same level of enthusiasm that I used to. It's like, I'll think about doing something fun, but then I'll just feel too tired or overwhelmed to actually follow through with it.

And it's not just big things, either. Even small things, like looking forward to a cup of coffee in the morning or a warm bath at night, just don't seem to bring me the same joy that they used to. It's like, I'm just going through the motions of taking care of myself and my baby, but I'm not really enjoying any of it. Which is sad, because I feel like I should be enjoying this time, you know? I'm a new mom, and this is supposed to be a happy time, but... I don't know, it just doesn't feel that way right now.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

.. yeah, that's definitely been me lately. I mean, if the baby cries, I immediately think it's because I'm not doing something right. Or if she's not gaining weight fast enough, I worry that it's because I'm not producing enough milk. It's like, I'll be sitting there, feeling fine, and then something will go wrong, and suddenly I'm flooded with thoughts of "I'm a bad mom" or "I'm not doing this right."

And it's not just the big things, either. Even little things, like if the house is messy or if I forget to do a load of laundry, I'll beat myself up over it. I'll think, "What kind of mom can't even keep her house clean?" or "What kind of mom forgets to do the laundry?" It's like, I'm constantly criticizing myself and feeling like I'm not good enough.

And the worst part is, I know it's not rational. I mean, I know that every mom makes mistakes, and that it's okay not to be perfect. But it's hard to shake the feeling that I'm somehow failing my baby, you know? It's like, I'll be sitting there, feeling anxious and worried, and I'll think to myself, "What if I'm not doing enough? What if I'm not giving my baby the best possible start in life?" And it's just this constant, nagging voice in the back of my head, always questioning my abilities as a mom.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, I'll think, "What if she's not getting enough to eat?" or "What if she's too hot or too cold?" And it's not even like I have any reason to think that, it's just this random worry that pops into my head.

And it's not just about the baby, either. I'll worry about my partner, too - like, what if they get hurt on the way home from work? Or I'll worry about the house - like, what if there's a fire or a break-in? It's just this constant, nagging sense of anxiety that's always there, even when everything is fine.

Sometimes it's hard to explain, because it's not like I'm worried about anything specific. It's just this general feeling of unease, like something is off or something is going to go wrong. And it's exhausting, because I feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to happen.

And the worst part is, I know it's not rational. I mean, I know that my baby is healthy and happy, and that my partner is fine, and that our house is safe. But it's hard to shake the feeling of anxiety, you know? It's like, my mind is always racing, always thinking about all the things that could go wrong, even when there's no reason to think that they will.

It's funny, because before the baby was born, I was never really an anxious person. I was always pretty laid-back and easy-going. But now, it's like, I'm constantly on high alert, waiting for something to go wrong. And it's hard to enjoy the moment, you know? Because I'm always worried about what's going to happen next.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, doing something normal, like feeding the baby or folding laundry, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. It's really scary, because I don't know what's happening or why I'm feeling that way.

Sometimes it's triggered by something small, like a noise or a movement. Like, if the baby makes a sudden cry, I'll feel this rush of adrenaline and my heart will start racing. Or if I'm walking down the stairs and I feel a little dizzy, I'll start to panic and think that I'm going to fall or something.

But other times, it just seems to come out of nowhere. I'll be sitting there, feeling fine, and then suddenly I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of fear or anxiety. It's like, my body is reacting to something, but I don't know what it is.

It's really hard to describe, because it's not like I'm afraid of anything specific. It's just this general feeling of dread or panic that takes over. And it's hard to shake, too. Sometimes it takes me a while to calm down and feel normal again.

I've tried to talk to my partner about it, but it's hard to explain. They just tell me to breathe deeply and try to relax, but it's not that easy. It's like, my body is responding to some kind of threat, even if there isn't one. And it's really frustrating, because I feel like I should be able to control my emotions, but I just can't seem to.

I guess it's just one of the many things that's been going on since the baby was born. I feel like my emotions are just all over the place, and I don't know how to deal with them. But it's nice to be able to talk about it, I guess. It feels like maybe I'm not just going crazy or something.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's definitely been true for me lately. I feel like everything is just piling up and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby is a 24/7 job, and it's exhausting. I mean, I love my baby, but it's just so much work. And on top of that, I'm still trying to recover from the birth, and my body is just not cooperating. I'm tired all the time, and I feel like I'm just going through the motions of taking care of myself and the baby.

And it's not just the physical stuff, either. Emotionally, I'm just feeling really overwhelmed. I feel like I'm supposed to be this perfect mom, and I'm just not living up to that. I'm making mistakes, and I'm worried that I'm not doing enough for my baby. And my partner is trying to be supportive, but I feel like they don't really get it. They're not the one who's up all night feeding the baby, or changing diapers all day.

Sometimes I just feel like I'm drowning in all of it. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and I'll just start to feel this sense of panic. Like, I don't know how I'm going to do this. I don't know how I'm going to take care of this tiny human who is completely dependent on me. And it's scary, because I feel like I'm not in control. I'm just reacting to everything, instead of being proactive.

I guess that's why I've been feeling so anxious and worried all the time. I just feel like things are getting on top of me, and I don't know how to get back on top of them. I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and it's exhausting. I just wish I could feel like myself again, you know? I wish I could feel confident and capable, instead of just feeling overwhelmed all the time.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been true for me lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and I think it's because I've just been feeling so unhappy and overwhelmed. I mean, I'm exhausted from taking care of the baby, but when I finally get a chance to sleep, my mind just starts racing. I'll lie there and think about all the things I need to do, or worry about the baby's health, or just feel anxious about everything.

And it's not just that I'm not sleeping well, it's that I'm not sleeping at all. I'll be up for hours in the middle of the night, just lying there and feeling miserable. And then when the baby wakes up, I'm already exhausted, so it's just this vicious cycle. I'm tired, but I'm also anxious and unhappy, so I just can't seem to relax and fall asleep.

I've tried to talk to my partner about it, but they just tell me to try to relax and that everything will be okay. But it's hard to relax when you're feeling so overwhelmed and unhappy. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of taking care of the baby and myself, but I'm not really living. I'm just existing, and it's a really sad and lonely feeling.

Sometimes I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and I'll just start to feel this wave of sadness wash over me. I'll think about how I used to be, before the baby was born, and how I used to feel. I was happy and carefree, and I didn't have all this anxiety and worry weighing me down. And it's hard not to feel like I've lost myself, you know? Like, I'm not the same person I used to be, and I don't know how to get back to that.

It's just really hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be happy and grateful for this new life, but instead I just feel overwhelmed and unhappy. And it's hard to admit that, because I feel like I'm supposed to be this perfect mom, and I'm just not living up to that. But it's nice to be able to talk about it, I guess. It feels like maybe I'm not just going crazy or something.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of taking care of the baby and myself, but I'm not really feeling anything positive. I'm just feeling sad and miserable, and I don't know how to get out of it. It's like, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or playing with her, and I'll just start to feel this wave of sadness wash over me. I'll think about how hard everything is, and how I'm not doing a good enough job, and it just feels like too much to handle.

Sometimes it's just a general feeling of sadness, and other times it's more specific. Like, I'll think about how my body is not recovering from the birth like I thought it would, or how I'm not bonding with the baby like I expected to. And it's hard not to feel like it's all my fault, you know? Like, I'm just not doing something right, and that's why I'm feeling this way.

It's funny, because before the baby was born, I was so excited to be a mom. I thought it would be this amazing, life-changing experience, and it is, but it's also really hard. And I feel like I'm just not prepared for how hard it is. I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and it's exhausting.

I've tried to talk to my partner about it, but they just tell me that everything is okay, and that I'm doing a great job. But it's hard to feel like I'm doing a great job when I'm feeling so sad and miserable all the time. I feel like I'm just pretending to be this happy, capable mom, but really I'm just struggling to get through each day.

It's nice to be able to talk about it, though. It feels like maybe I'm not just going crazy or something. Maybe I'm just feeling what a lot of new moms feel, and that's okay. But it's hard to shake the feeling that I'm just not doing enough, and that everything is my fault.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been crying a lot, and it's not just because I'm tired or overwhelmed, although that's part of it. It's just that I feel so sad and unhappy, and I don't know how to make it stop. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start to feel this wave of emotion wash over me. I'll think about how hard everything is, and how I'm not doing a good enough job, and it just feels like too much to handle.

And then I'll start to cry, and it's not just a few tears, either. I'm talking about full-on, sobbing, can't-catch-my-breath crying. It's like, my body is just releasing all this pent-up emotion, and I don't know how to stop it. It's scary, because I feel like I'm losing control, and I don't know how to get it back.

It's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be this strong, capable mom, and crying just doesn't fit into that image. But at the same time, I feel like I'm just being honest, you know? I'm acknowledging that this is hard, and that I'm struggling, and that it's okay to not be okay.

I've tried to talk to my partner about it, but they just tell me that everything is going to be okay, and that I'm doing a great job. But it's hard to feel like I'm doing a great job when I'm crying all the time. I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and it's exhausting.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that it's nice to be able to talk about this, and to know that I'm not alone. It feels like maybe I'm not just going crazy, or that I'm not just a bad mom. Maybe I'm just a mom who's struggling, and that's okay.
